subject.title: macOS launchd Gateway still restarts via gateway-update/update.run; document and honor auto-update kill-switch

question: Should `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` block only configured background `update.auto` applies, or should it also block supervised Gateway `update.run` handoffs from the control plane on headless installs?
rationale: Current code, docs, and tests deliberately split automatic startup/background applies from explicit `update.run`; changing that split affects operator-requested updates, availability recovery, and update safety semantics.

options.title: Keep the current split
options.body: Document that `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE` blocks configured background applies only, while explicit `update.run` reliability stays on the launchd update tracker.

options.title: Broaden the env kill-switch
options.body: Make supervised `update.run` refuse before managed handoff when `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1`, and update docs/tests/live proof for that new contract.

options.title: Add a separate update.run policy
options.body: Introduce a distinct operator-controlled setting for control-plane update handoffs instead of overloading the existing auto-update kill-switch.

recommendation.title: Keep the current split
recommendation.body: Document that `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE` blocks configured background applies only, while explicit `update.run` reliability stays on the launchd update tracker.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc introduced the kill-switch behavior and has recent issue-review context on the macOS update.run handoff proof boundary.
